items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation at the open — went straight into video/inventory review
Did not ask about box count, additional stops, or access concerns (parking/elevator/HOA) — customer had to raise the complex handover himself
Never asked the moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
No 'pricing is super simple' framing before quoting the $95/mover rate
Never stated what's included — gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools
No packing materials pricing given even though packing the bookcase/books is part of the job
No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) never mentioned — a real gap on a move with a mounted TV, a large painting and a tilted bookcase
No 'no hidden fees' pitch (no CC fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees)
Clock mechanics only half explained — 2.5 hr minimum stated, but not that the clock starts on-site at contract open, and no 15-minute prorated increments
No 'does that make sense?' sense-check anywhere in the call
Truck count never stated in the estimate
No Save Your Ass prep speech — no consolidation examples (toys, garden tools, loose drawer items, wall photos), no 'take a carload' tip, no close
Confirmation email handoff never explained — no mention of an email, no bolded detail list, no 'reply with any corrections'
No 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Business hours never given (only 'call us later' and 'this number')
top_strength: The inventory verification off the walkthrough video was genuinely thorough — she worked room by room, named specific items (dumbbells, credenza, large painting, tall cabinet, tilted bookcase), and proactively surfaced the TV-mounting question with a clean answer (we can unmount, we can't remount at the new place). She also anchored the estimate against his prior move with Einstein, which made the 6-8 hour / 3-mover / $2,555 number credible instead of arbitrary.
coaching_note: Joanna closed the booking but skipped every differentiator — No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee and the no-hidden-fees pitch were all absent, and the only value framing she gave was 'you only pay for how long it takes.' On this call in particular, damage coverage was the obvious one to lead with: a wall-mounted TV, a large painting and a full bookcase of books are exactly the items customers worry about. Repeat customers are not a reason to drop the pitch — Sonny had a competitor move his sofa and chairs last time, so this was a live win-back moment. Add a 30-second differentiator block right after the hourly rate, every call, and pair it with the Save Your Ass prep speech (consolidate loose items, take a carload) which she also skipped entirely despite quoting a packing job.
phone_presence_notes: Warm, patient and reassuring throughout — the customer ended with 'I love you guys' and 'Joanna, you're awesome' — though her own language leaned heavily on filler affirmations ('Mm-hmm', 'of course') rather than varied, specific acknowledgment.
